children: SYDNEY--A lack of diversification in investment grade non-financial corporate bonds going forward could stoke increased market volatility, Fitch Ratings warned in a report Wednesday.
Issuance is becoming increasingly concentrated in the technology, telecommunications and retail sectors as highly rated hyperscalers issue debt to help fund investment, Fitch said.

Increased volatility could lead to tighter funding conditions for some issuers, especially if Treasury yields remain elevated and hyperscaler credit profiles or equity valuations weaken causing spreads to widen, Fitch added.

The market environment could amplify risk for issuers in sectors such as healthcare, technology and utilities that have significant upcoming maturities, due to higher borrowing costs and the need to time issuance opportunistically when refinancing this debt, it said.
Non-financial investment-grade corporate bond issuance in the U.S. totalled $940 billion in the year to end-October, up 33% on the same period last year, the ratings agency said.

Significant AI-linked debt issuance will likely continue over the near term but could become more sporadic if uncertainty related to returns on AI-related investment continues and investor demand ebbs and flows, Fitch added.

Despite an expected increase in regulation of the AI sector under a Democrat-dominated U.S. Congress, Fitch said the uncertainty is unlikely to lead to a major pullback in investment in 2027, Fitch said.
Total issuance is on track to peak at around $3 trillion in 2027, it added.

title: AI Issuance Could Raise Corporate Bond Market Volatility, Says Fitch
